title: Replace your note apps with a text folder your agent files
summary: A poster moved tasks, meeting notes and client details from six apps into one text-file folder; Claude Code reads a map file daily and files new notes on approval.
agent_role: Claude Code reads a map file at the start of each session. After a conversation, the user types /save and Claude proposes which files to update; the user approves before it writes.
outcome: Author reports replacing 6 apps and 3 subscriptions at no cost beyond the Claude plan, with full history kept in Git.
what_they_did: The poster moved all their notes into one folder of plain text files on their computer. It has subfolders for notes, people, projects, an inbox and an archive. A file called CLAUDE.md acts as a map that Claude Code reads every session. After a useful chat they type /save, Claude shows which files it wants to change, and they approve. Obsidian opens the same folder as a nicer viewer.
how_it_went: They say it replaced six apps, three subscriptions and an unused Notion workspace. They also say it costs nothing beyond their Claude plan and keeps full history through Git.
worth_knowing: The trade-off is real: there is no slick mobile widget and no shared workspace with comments.
prompt: Help me set up a notes folder at [folder path] with subfolders for notes, people, projects, inbox and archive. Write a CLAUDE.md map file that explains where each kind of information lives. At the start of each session, read the map. When I type /save after a conversation, list the files you want to create or update and what you will write. Wait for my OK before changing anything.

curation.rationale: A real setup in which Claude Code files notes into a plain-text folder after the user approves. It is a fairly common pattern, and the full details sit in a linked article that was not provided.
